rationale: Narrow, fully-specified errno semantics over a tiny implementation surface. fsync03 asserts exactly five cases: fsync() must fail EINVAL on a pipe fd, EINVAL on an AF_UNIX socket fd, EBADF on a closed fd, EBADF on fd -1, and EINVAL on a fifo fd. Asterinas' whole implementation is 27 lines (kernel/src/syscall/fsync.rs); sys_fsync resolves the fd then calls file.as_inode_handle_or_err()?.path().sync_all(). as_inode_handle_or_err already yields EINVAL, so the pipe and socket cases should already be satisfied and the likely single defect is the fifo case: a fifo opened by path is backed by an InodeHandle, so the downcast succeeds and sync_all() returns Ok(0) where Linux returns EINVAL. That points at one missing file-type check rather than a subsystem Asterinas lacks. Supporting evidence from this run: fsync03 passes on the host (LTP 20260529) and fails in Asterinas on 68bdd4a99, while its siblings fsync01 and fsync02 both pass in Asterinas, so the fsync path works for regular files and only the non-syncable-file-type boundary is wrong. The failure is a clean assert failure, not a setup break, so mkfifo/pipe/AF_UNIX socket all work in Asterinas. Chosen over the other narrow finalists: dup03/dup06 (EMFILE on a full fd table) need RLIMIT_NOFILE enforcement in the fd allocation path, a wider blast radius; llseek01 needs RLIMIT_FSIZE plus SIGXFSZ delivery, which is a subsystem rather than a check. Preferred a genuine localized defect over the 35 stale pool entries this run measured as already passing, since those reduce to a pool edit with no kernel change.
notes: First run of this skill: select.cache was empty and run-7UHmXC is the only run under .fix-conformance/, so nothing was already covered. Cached 367 records total (245 host observations at LTP version 20260529, plus 122 probe/stale-entry records at commit 68bdd4a99). Candidate derivation: of 976 commented-out all.txt entries, 306 have an already-enabled numeric sibling; 254 survived dropping subsystems Asterinas plainly lacks; 234 of those passed on the host; 104 were then probed in Asterinas across 5 boots. fsync04 stays commented out on line 451 and fsync01 on line 448 - this run enables only line 450. Two things the later phases should know. First, an important probing constraint: batches of ~79 and ~30 selector entries both panicked the kernel with 'called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: NoMemory' at kernel/libs/ring-buffer/src/lib.rs:104 (RingBuffer::new -> alloc_segment) after 60-80s of cumulative testing, despite 8G of guest RAM; fallocate05 was the entry in flight for one of them. This looks like cumulative memory pressure across many tests in one boot rather than a single test's bug, it is unrelated to fsync03, and it is why probing was chunked. Keep verify's single-test runs small and do not read this panic as an fsync03 regression. Second, kirk's stdout is redirected to a log file that run_ltp_test.sh only cats after the run completes, so a mid-run kernel panic loses every per-test result. This phase temporarily changed that redirect to a tee to stream results, took its measurements, and reverted the file; the worktree is clean except for the expected untracked .osdk/. If a later phase needs per-test visibility through a panic it will have to make the same temporary edit and revert it. Also note kirk reports 'broken' for a failed test setup and 'skip' for unsupported preconditions; only pass and fail/broken were cached, skips were not, since skip maps to neither cache value. Host baseline excluded 20 candidates: 8 timeouts under a 20s host cap (bind06, creat05, fork13, futex_wake04, open04, preadv203, select02, writev03), 8 tconf, 2 tbroke, ftruncate04 fail, and mmap22 SIGSEGV; the timeout and rc139 ones were left out of the cache because neither maps to one of the four valid host result values.
